title: tier-2 shipped code: the client's SWAR strlen against 0x1426cce30
notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-casc/src/bytes.rs::client_strlen, built by cargo and called by crates/ow-casc/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the client_strlen entry. The ledger binds the verdict to bytes.rs + the probe source + the git revision. The function is the length helper the encoding espec build calls (0x142498a70); 1,628 call sites reach it.

Oracle is strlen at exe 0x1426cce30, extent 0x1426cce30..0x1426cced8 (168 bytes through the ret at 0x1426cced7), which is the declared coverageWindow. v2b 0x7ff7c73ece30 is 0x7ff7c4d20000 + (0x1426cce30 - 0x140000000). Signature: (const char *s) -> size_t length (RCX -> RAX).

The read, instruction for instruction: `neg rcx` turns the start into `-s`, so the return is `end - s` (the length), not the terminator's address. The client first walks an unaligned start a byte at a time (`test al, 7` / `jne` at 0x1426cce36/0x1426cce49) until `al & 7 == 0` or a NUL is found (`test dl, dl` / `je` at 0x1426cce45), then reads one qword at a time: `r9 = 0x7efefefefefefeff + x`, `t = (~x) ^ r9`, `t &= 0x8101010101010100` (0x1426cce4d..0x1426cce77); a zero `t` loops to the next qword. On a hit the qword is reloaded and the first zero byte is found from the low byte up (0x1426cce79..0x1426ccea6); the return is `qword_address + 8 - s - (8 - j)`, i.e. the byte offset of the NUL. A flagged qword with no zero byte falls through the `test dh, dh` / `jne` at 0x1426ccea6 and loops to the next qword.

The test is not a perfect zero-byte detector: some qwords with no zero byte are flagged (the fixture's FP qword, 0x803982c75afe2a0f, is one). The client's byte scan then finds no zero and loops, so the returned length is still the true one; the Rust reproduces the exact test and the same fall-through, so the two agree on those inputs rather than one of them being a byte scan.

The client's byte walk is a performance path: the test is a correct detector and the byte scan finds the first NUL, so the returned length is the same for every alignment. The Rust reads qwords from index 0 and records that equivalence here, the same way fn/Memcmp records its byte scan; the fixture varies the oracle's alignment through `arena_offset` to exercise the client's walk, and the differential compares the length only.

Compared channels: the 64-bit return (the client's RAX value) and the 0x100-byte pointee. The client writes nothing; the probe returns the buffer unchanged, so any write would show as a pointee divergence.

The fixture's declared cases walk every branch: an empty string at each alignment 0..7 (the byte walk's NUL exit); a NUL at each byte 0..7 of the first qword, aligned (the byte scan's seven `je` edges and the byte-7 `jne` not-taken edge); unaligned starts 1..7 with the NUL before and after the alignment point (both edges of the walk's `jne`); several qwords before the NUL (the SWAR `je` loop back edge); and a flagged qword with no zero byte followed by a NUL (the byte scan's `jne` taken edge). The sweep after that varies the alignment, the NUL position and the fill pattern.

Coverage: the 168-byte window holds twelve conditional branch sites - the initial alignment test, the byte walk's NUL test and alignment back edge, the SWAR zero test, the seven byte-scan `je` tests and the byte-7 `jne`. All twelve are driven to both edges by the declared cases, so the gate is 100%.
allowedImageReads is empty: the function reads only its buffer - no image constants, no call, no cookie (the body is a leaf).

knownEquivalentMutants.rationale: `while shift < 64` over `shift = 0, 8, ..., 56`. The widened `shift <= 64` runs one extra iteration at shift 64, where `(x >> 64) & 0xff` is `x & 0xff` (Rust masks the shift amount in release). That iteration can only return when byte 0 is zero, but the byte scan reaches shift 64 only after bytes 0..6 were all nonzero and byte 7 was nonzero - i.e. the qword holds no zero byte. So byte 0 is nonzero, the extra iteration does not return, and the loop exits at shift 72 exactly as the original exits at shift 64. No input can observe the boundary change. Line updated from 99 to 100 when the doc comment above the function gained a line.

acknowledgedGaps.why: The client reads until a NUL with no bounds check; a buffer with none would run off the caller's buffer. The fixture always places a NUL inside the 0x100-byte buffer, and the Rust returns the offset it reached rather than panicking, so a mutant that loses the NUL answers differently instead of faulting.

acknowledgedGaps.what: the candidate's pointer alignment is not the oracle's
acknowledgedGaps.why: The client's byte walk is selected by the absolute address's low three bits. The harness's candidate buffer does not carry the arena address, so the Rust reads qwords from index 0 instead of aligning first. The zero-byte test is a fast detector (its false positives are handled by the byte scan's fall-through) and the byte scan is exact, so the returned length is the same for every alignment; the fixture varies the oracle's alignment through `arena_offset` to exercise the client's walk, and the differential compares the length only.
